 Judgment
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Smt. Lakshmidevamma, in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. That, on 16.12.2023 at about 11-40 p.m, when the deceased was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50/S-2576 as a pillion rider near Nilagumba village, Gudibande Taluk, Chikkaballapura District, rider of said vehicle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and got jumped, by that time, the deceased fell down and sustained severe injuries all over the body.

Immediately she was shifted to Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura for first aid, then referred to NIMHANS hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment and again she was sent back to Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura for further treatment, wherein she took treatment as inpatient and died on the way to Sapthagiri hospital.

Subsequently, the petitioners have spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body,
funeral and obsequies ceremonies of the deceased and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the deceased was aged about 65 years and doing agriculture and coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and contributing entire income to the maintenance of the family.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners are put to lot of mental agony and untold misery.
4. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50/S-2576.
Hence, Gudibanda Police have registered a criminal case against rider of said offending vehicle in Cr.No.03/2024.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
5. After service of the notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal, remained absent and hence he was placed exparte.
The 5 SCCH-18 MVC No. 889/2024 respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
6. The respondent No.2 in the written statement contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50/S-2576 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is contended that, the rider of the said vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further contended that offending vehicle is not at all involved in the alleged accident, the petitioners falsely implicated the same in the accident.
It is further contended that, deceased was not died due to accidental injuries and there is no nexus between the injuries sustained by the deceased and her death.
She died due to some other ailment and not due to accidental injuries, it is a natural death.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased and relationship of petitioners with deceased.
It is also contention of the respondent that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition, against the respondent No.2.
7.

On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this court had framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that Smt. Lakshmidevamma died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 16-12-2023 at about 11-40 p.m. near Nilagumba village, Gudibande Taluk, Chikkaballapura Dist., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle b earing Reg.No.KA-50/S-2576 in an actionable negligence?

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 50/S-2576, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Smt. Lakshmidevamma died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.
On the contrary, the respondent No.2 contended that, the offending vehicle is not at all involved in the alleged accident, the petitioners falsely implicated the same in the accident.
It is further contended that, deceased was died due to self fall and not the accidental injuries and there is no nexus between the injuries sustained by the deceased and her death.
15. In such a situation, it is necessary to go through the evidence available on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion with respect to the above point in issue.
On going through the above issue, burden is on the petitioners to prove the same on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.

RW2 has deposed in his evidence that as per the police records the alleged accident was taken place on 16.12.2023, but the complaint was lodged on 4.1.2024 and as per the hospital records it was a non-MLC case.
The respondent No.1 is a close relative of the petitioners and the petitioners have made a false case against the motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-S-2576 and falsely implicated the same.
In the cross-examination he has admitted that in Ex.P18 self fall has been mentioned.
At the same time, in billing type MLC has been mentioned.
In Ex.P22 issued by NIMHANS the history of injured written as 'RTA two wheeler'.
Further denied the suggestion that till her death she was taking treatment.
20. It is not in dispute that the accident in question was taken place on 16.12.2023 and the complaint was lodged on 4.1.2024.
Merely because, there is some delay in lodging the complaint, it cannot be the ground to reject the claim petition.
21. On perusal of evidence of RW1 and Ex.P18, though the respondents have examined the author of the document, but it cannot be said that the accident was not occurred.
Moreover, on perusal of Ex.P22, it is clear that the accident occurred due to RTA from two wheeler.
The respondent No.2 has not made on effort to examine either the rider of the offending vehicle or any eye witness, who witnessed the alleged accident.
Except examination of RW1, he has not challenged the police papers filed against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-S-2576.
Hence, the contention taken by the respondent No.2 cannot be accepted.

22. Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.2 about the denial of allegation made against the rider of the offending vehicle.
23. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA- 50-S-2576 and in the said accident, Lakshmidevamma succumbed to the injuries.
13 SCCH-18 MVC No. 889/2024

ISSUE No.2;
24.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

sentences.text: Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the husband has lost his wife and the petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased have lost their love and affection of their mother, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
26. In the case on hand, no doubt the petitioner No.2 to 4 are children of the deceased Lakshmidevamma.
According to them, they were dependents to the deceased petitioners during her lifetime.
No contra materials are available on record to show that, they were not dependents to their mother during her lifetime.
Here, it is necessary discuss the point that, father/mother place an important role in the family.
All the children, one or the other way defendants to their parents whether they are minors or majors, married or unmarried.
But the percentage of disability may be varied from one person to another person.
During the minority of the child, dependency is more on the parents.
After the marriage of the children, the percentage of disability is less on the parents, if compare with the minor children.

27. In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though they are major sons, they could have dependents to their parents not only economically, but, in connection with love and affection during his lifetime.
Hence, the petitioners can be presumed as 15 SCCH-18 MVC No. 889/2024 dependents to their father during his lifetime in the absence of contra materials from the other side.
28. The Division Bench of Supreme Court, in National Insurance Company Limited V/S Birender and Others stated that, a major and earning son has a right to claim compensation under Motor Vehicle Act.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/S Birender and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, by referring the case of Manjuri Bera, stated that, even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant if he was a legal representative will be entitled to compensation.

Even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation, and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application,
irrespective of the fact, whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
29.
The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P16 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the year of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 1956.
The accident occurred on 16.12.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 67 years.
For his age, multiplier '5' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.
30. In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing agriculture and coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But in support of definite income of the deceased, there is no iota of documents to show that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

In case the deceased was self-employed or on 17 SCCH-18 MVC No. 889/2024 a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

"
32. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
33.
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are four persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
34. In the present case, deceased was aged about 67 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "5" is applicable.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,92,000/- per year.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,44,000/- (Rs.1,92,000-Rs.48,000).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "5" which comes to Rs.7,20,000/-.
35.

O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.9,31,500/- (Rupees nine lakh thirty one thousand and five hundred only) along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Smt. Lakshmidevamma, in a road traffic accident.
Hence, Gudibanda Police have registered a criminal case against rider of said offending vehicle in Cr.No.03/2024.
opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this court had framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that Smt. Lakshmidevamma died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 16-12-2023 at about 11-40 p.m. near Nilagumba village, Gudibande Taluk, Chikkaballapura Dist., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle b earing Reg.No.KA-50/S-2576 in an actionable negligence?
